text: , summarise precursor-level data non-enriched runs protein intensities using maxLFQ, one default methods used DIA data analysis. Note, maxLFQ implementation can become slow large datasets. case recommend median polish method. maxLFQ first calculates pairwise log ratio’s samples using shared precursors. Particularly, uses median log ratio’s shared precursors, .e.  rij=median(ysj−ysi)r_{ij} = median(y_{sj}-y_{si}). Hence, first eliminates ion effects. estimates summaries solving ∑∑j(yjprot−yiprot−rij)2 \sum_i\sum_j(y^{prot}_j - y^{prot}_i - r_ij)^2 implemented maxLFQ function iq package. aggregateFeatures() QFeatures package streamlines summarisation. requires name rowData column group precursors proteins (protein groups), Protein.Group. provide summarisation approach fun argument. function return QFeatures object new set called proteins. summarisation methods available MsCoreUtils package, see ?aggregateFeatures comprehensive list.

code: calculate_usage <- function(qf,                            i_ptm,                            i_ne,                            contrasts,                            fcol_ptm = "Protein.Group",                            fcol_ne = "Protein.Group",                             satterthwaite = FALSE) {   match_precursor_to_protein_FC <- match(rowData(qf[[i_ptm]])[[fcol_ptm]],                                          rowData(qf[[i_ne]])[[fcol_ne]]) #1.    for (contrast in contrasts)     {     results_ne <- rowData(qf[[i_ne]])[[contrast]] #2.1     colnames(results_ne) <- results_ne |>        colnames() |>        paste0("_ne")     rowData(qf[[i_ptm]])[[contrast]] <- cbind(       rowData(qf[[i_ptm]])[[contrast]],        results_ne[match_precursor_to_protein_FC,]) |> #2.2        mutate(         logUsage = logFC - logFC_ne, #2.3         se_usage = sqrt(se^2 + se_ne^2),         t_usage = logUsage /se_usage,         df_usage = if (satterthwaite) (se^2 + se_ne^2)^2/(se^4/df + se_ne^4/df_ne) else df,         pval_usage = pt(abs(t_usage), df_usage, lower.tail = FALSE)*2,          adjPval_usage = p.adjust(pval_usage, method = "fdr")         )   }     return(qf) } qf <- calculate_usage(qf, i_ptm = "precursorsPTM_norm", i_ne = "proteins", contrasts = colnames(L)) inferencesUsage <-    msqrobCollect(qf[["precursorsPTM_norm"]], L) |>    relocate(contains("sage"))

text: , summarise precursor-level data non-enriched runs protein intensities using maxLFQ, one default methods used DIA data analysis. Note, maxLFQ implementation can become slow large datasets. case recommend median polish method. maxLFQ first calculates pairwise log ratio’s samples using shared precursors. Particularly, uses median log ratio’s shared precursors, .e.  rij=median(ysj−ysi)r_{ij} = median(y_{sj}-y_{si}). Hence, first eliminates ion effects. estimates summaries solving ∑∑j(yjprot−yiprot−rij)2 \sum_i\sum_j(y^{prot}_j - y^{prot}_i - r_ij)^2 implemented maxLFQ function iq package. aggregateFeatures() QFeatures package streamlines summarisation. requires name rowData column group precursors proteins (protein groups), Protein.Group. provide summarisation approach fun argument. function return QFeatures object new set called proteins. summarisation methods available MsCoreUtils package, see ?aggregateFeatures comprehensive list.
